title: Jonah and the Summer
premise: Ansel Quintana inherited a bankrupt vineyard and a habit of keeping everyone at arm's length, rebuilding his life one careful season at a time. When a freak June snowstorm traps him in the estate's old farmhouse with Marisol Vega—the rival winemaker who broke his heart a decade ago—and Theo Brandt, the developer circling his land, three days of forced proximity crack open everything he buried. As the thaw comes, Ansel must choose between selling the vineyard to escape his debts or betting the whole harvest, and his whole heart, on a first vintage he might lose. He stays, plants, and risks it all; the book ends at the first harvest festival, where Ansel, having finally chosen love over safety, toasts a modest but real future with Marisol while Theo walks away empty-handed.
about_author: Wendell Villalobos is a former sommelier who traded restaurant cellars for a writing desk in wine country, where he now chronicles second chances among the vines. His fiction blends agricultural realism with slow-burn romance, drawing on years of listening to growers argue about weather, money, and regret.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Three years after inheriting Quintana Vineyards—mortgaged, half-dead, and short-staffed—Ansel audits what little he has left before winter. The beat establishes his careful, small-step philosophy and the quiet loneliness beneath his competence.

chapters.title: The Man Who Buys Hillsides
chapters.summary: Theo Brandt arrives with an offer for the land, all charm and spreadsheets. Ansel's POV. He refuses without explaining why, and we learn the vineyard is less a business than a promise to his late grandmother. Beat: stubbornness as armor.

chapters.title: Marisol, Unannounced
chapters.summary: Marisol Vega appears at the county tasting fair, her award-winning label two rows from Ansel's folding table. His POV. A decade ago they were lovers and co-conspirators; now she's the rival whose success stings most. Beat: old wounds reopened by politeness.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, flashback woven through present-day pruning. We see how their romance collapsed when Marisol took the job across the valley and Ansel chose invisibility over following her. Beat: understanding that his caution was born of that loss.

chapters.title: A Forecast No One Believed
chapters.summary: June snow is forecast—a once-in-a-century storm. Ansel races to protect the young vines and finds Marisol already in his cellar, stranded after her car died on the pass. His POV. Beat: panic sharpened by unwanted company.

chapters.title: Three at the Farmhouse
chapters.summary: Theo's truck slides into the ditch; now all three are trapped together. Alternating POV, Ansel-led. Power outages force candlelight, shared meals, and a chessboard with grudges attached. Beat: comedy of forced intimacy masking tension.

chapters.title: What Theo Wants
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Over brandy, he reveals his own history: a family farm lost to debt, which is why he buys failing ones—to save them from worse. Ansel hears himself in the enemy. Beat: sympathy complicating opposition.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake of Their Twenties
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Snowbound memories surface: the summer she and Ansel made a wild, unlicensed wine in his grandmother's cellar—the mistake that taught them both everything. Beat: tenderness rekindling under old resentment.

chapters.title: Night Two
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A near-kiss interrupted by a collapsing trellis alarm sends them into the freezing rows to save the vines side by side. Working shoulder to shoulder, words fail and hands don't. Beat: bodies remembering what minds deny.

chapters.title: Marisol's Side of the Break
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She confesses why she really left: not ambition, but fear that staying would make her small like Ansel had chosen to be. The accusation lands hard. Beat: truth as a weapon and a gift.

chapters.title: The Thaw
chapters.summary: The storm breaks; roads reopen. Theo leaves first with a revised offer and a deadline: thirty days. Marisol lingers, then goes too, leaving a bottle of their old 'mistake' wine on the porch. Ansel's POV. Beat: the house too quiet again.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. He inventories the damage, the debt, and the math Theo sent. Selling would end the pressure forever; harvesting means borrowing against everything. Beat: the cost of safety made explicit.

chapters.title: Found Hands
chapters.summary: Neighbors, seasonal workers, and Marisol's crew chief arrive to help with storm-damaged vines—unpaid, unprompted. Ansel's POV realizes he built more community than he knew. Beat: found family arriving before he asks.

chapters.title: Lending Pieces
chapters.summary: Marisol returns 'to inspect frost damage,' clearly lying. Ansel's POV. They work the east block and negotiate a truce: friendship first, no promises. Both know it's a lie they're agreeing to tell. Beat: cautious re-entry.

chapters.title: Veraison
chapters.summary: The grapes begin to ripen; so does the relationship. Marisol's POV. First kiss in the same cellar as the old mistake, deliberately remade. Beat: joy shadowed by the ticking thirty-day clock.

chapters.title: Theo's Last Card
chapters.summary: Theo reveals the bank called his loan on Ansel's debt—he can buy it or let a vulture fund do worse. Ansel's POV. Betrayal and a terrible choice: sign now or gamble the harvest. Beat: rising dread.

chapters.title: The Fight in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Marisol discovers Ansel secretly prepared sale papers to protect her from being entangled in his ruin. Her POV. She throws his caution back at him: loving in installments is just another way of leaving. Beat: climax of the heart.

chapters.title: All In
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Dawn decision: he tears up the papers, signs the high-risk harvest loan, and drives through the valley to ask Marisol—not for forgiveness, but for partnership in every sense. Beat: the whole heart risked.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. The community gathers for picking; Theo watches from the ridge, unexpectedly moved. Ansel offers him something better than a sale: a partnership in the next planting, on honest terms. Beat: power offered rather than taken.

chapters.title: First Pressing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The crush begins; numbers are tight but real. Theo declines the partnership but withdraws his bid, leaving a note: 'Some things shouldn't be bought.' Beat: antagonist humanized, stakes resolved.

chapters.title: The Festival
chapters.summary: Harvest festival under string lights. Ansel publicly thanks the found family that saved the vineyard, then privately gives Marisol a bottle labeled with next year's date—a promise measured in seasons, not steps. Beat: love declared without hedging.

chapters.title: Jonah and the Summer
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Ansel's POV. Named for the stubborn vine that survived the snow, the first bottled vintage sits beside the old 'mistake' wine. Marisol's toothbrush is in the farmhouse bathroom. Beat: quiet, earned resolution—memory honored, future planted.
